_note: Two defects on c1_whitepaper were cancelling each other, and each alone measured within2pt 0.0000 in BOTH parser arms -- on the gated fixture that stands in for the document class this converter exists for. `before` is the 7154669 converter; `after` is the same tree with `options.ladder` defaulted on and `infer.FIG_MERGE_GAP` raised 4.0 -> 6.0. The two commits between the audit and this landing (832a5eb, 7154669) touched testkit, docs and evidence only -- no file under exactdoc/ -- so the `before` column measured at 2948e4b describes 7154669 unchanged. Both columns measured in the canonical container, same corpus, same profiles. This record also carries the RAW-LANE BASELINE RE-RECORD: c1's page_err and word_recall improved past their recorded values, a gate that fails on improvement needs its record moved, and the move was made deliberately here rather than absorbed silently.
adjudication: Landed as one commit on coordinator adjudication. The two changes are inseparable: see `cancellation` below.

D-A._note: Shared by both parser arms. This is the whole of the within2pt 0.0000 -- a constant offset no word escaped.
D-A.arms: pdfium and pymupdf, identical to 0.01pt above the card row
cause_chain: c1's cover band is a Chromium full-bleed fill inset to y0=7.16; `detect_hf.top_bands` seeds only on y0 <= 2.5, so cover_band is None and the band ships as an ordinary in-flow `box` table.

The band cell holds ONE paragraph carrying two source lines: a 9.77pt title and an 8.0pt subtitle. `_split_lines_to_paras` splits on a dominant-size ratio over 1.3 (9.77/8.00 = 1.221) or a baseline gap over max(lead*1.55, lead+4) = 26.3pt (the gap is 16.94pt). Neither fires.
The renderer sets both runs on one line. The row renders 98.15pt against a declared 112.68pt.
Every element below inherits the lost line.

subtitle_signature._note: The subtitle sitting on the title's line is the defect made visible.

D-A.fix: options.ladder default False -> True. The ladder already computed this case correctly (predict_lines -> 1 against src_lines 2, _lock -> True, inserts the soft break); it simply never ran in any profile.

D-B._note: PyMuPDF only. PDFium reports a stroke ring outside each card fill, merged the row on its own, and showed no step -- the two arms disagreeing was itself the evidence that the row is one figure.
cause_chain: c1's three rounded-corner stat cards share an exact source y-extent (222.2..279.5) and sit in 9.33pt gutters.
After `build_figure`'s own +/-2pt clip padding the surviving gap is 5.3pt; `_merge_figures` expanded by 4.0pt and missed by 1.3pt.
Three block-level FigureEls stack vertically: 171pt of flow against the source's 57pt.
D-B.fix: infer.FIG_MERGE_GAP 4.0 -> 6.0. Clears 5.3 with margin, still far below the 9.33pt raw gutter.

D-C._note: OUT OF SCOPE, characterised and left. Now the sole driver of c1's remaining dy_p90.
D-C.finding: Page 2's first paragraph carries space_before=1050 twips (52.5pt). The writer emits it correctly -- verified in word/document.xml, p41 -- and the renderer drops w:spacing w:before at the top of a page after a hard break. The page-break carrier paragraph (p40) is 1pt exact with before=0.
D-C.shape_of_fix: Emit a page-top leading gap as an explicit spacer paragraph rather than relying on w:before, as the writer already does for chunk pre-gaps. Needs live Google Docs evidence to scope: whether Docs drops it too is unmeasured, and the proxy-mispredicts rule forbids promoting a gdocs compensation on LibreOffice evidence.

D-D._note: OUT OF SCOPE, characterised and left.
D-D.finding: Residual horizontal drift dominates within2pt once D-A and D-B are fixed: dx_p50 2.62 overall, with justified lines at dx 25-38. This is a re-wrap problem, untouched here, and it is why c1's within2pt lands at 0.10-0.14 rather than near 1.0 despite dy_p50 2.0.

cancellation._note: Why the two changes are one commit. Fixing D-A alone REMOVES a -11.7pt error that had been partly hiding a +115pt one, so the composite metric gets worse while the document gets strictly more correct at the top. Measured, not reasoned.
cancellation.ladder_alone_gate: FAIL (raw): 2 findings, both REGRESSIONS on c1 -- dy_p50 101 -> 116.2 and word_recall 0.797 -> 0.7667.

isolation._note: Per-line displacement maps, c1 only, open loop. The field is a flat constant plus one step -- not a leading-model error and not accumulating. Measured at the standard profile (exact line mode), which is the encoding LibreOffice is calibrated for; the ramp visible at the gdocs profile is the multiple-encoding-through-LibreOffice artifact and is not a real error.

field_by_source_y._note: src_y -2 is page 2, which D-C still owns.

gate._note: testkit/runall.py, both lanes, canonical container. Zero regressions across all 32 cells (16 documents x 2 lanes); 24 cells byte-identical. The `after` numbers are the re-recorded baseline, and the verification run below gates against them.

baseline_rerecord._note: A HEADLINE EVENT, not a footnote. Recording an improvement is still moving a gate's floor, and the reason has to survive the commit that did it.
baseline_rerecord.why: With both fixes live the raw lane reported gate FAIL with 2 findings, both STALE rather than regressions: c1's page_err cleared 0 but was recorded as 1, and its word_recall reached 0.9697 against a recorded 0.797. A stale record re-admits the regression it exists to catch, so the gate correctly refuses to pass until the record is moved.
baseline_rerecord.method: GATE_BASELINE=update testkit/runall.py (clears the record, then gates the same run against the empty one, so its findings are informational and its exit code proves nothing), CHAINED with a second plain testkit/runall.py that gates against the record just written.
baseline_rerecord._direction_note: Every moved value improves. No recorded floor was lowered.

collateral_improvements._note: Not targeted, and the reason this change is NOT c1-scoped -- which is why it needed adjudication rather than a quiet landing.
collateral_improvements.c4_i18n.pdf: within2pt 0.1966 -> 0.5043 in BOTH lanes. Its CJK/RTL lines are re-wrap-sensitive and the ladder pins them.
collateral_improvements.l1_word_native.pdf: product dy_p50 14.69 -> 0.01 and word_recall 0.9931 -> 1.0; raw dy_p50 26.69 -> 2.71. A PDF printed from a word processor is exactly the case where source line breaks are authoritative.

live_prediction._note: FOR THE LIVE-PASS LEDGER. A PREDICTION, NOT A RESULT. Per the standing rule, a gdocs-profile change is never promoted on LibreOffice-proxy evidence alone; this entry exists to be confirmed or falsified by a live pass, and must not be cited as a measurement until then.
live_prediction.advisory: c1_marginal (dy_p50 9.30 against a policy bound of 10) should clear comfortably if the prediction holds.
live_prediction.reasoning: D-A is a structural line-count error in the document -- a row that renders one line shorter than the source -- not a line-metric translation. It should therefore transfer to Google Docs rather than being a proxy artifact. The proxy's own before-number at the gdocs profile (10.28) sits close to the recorded live 9.30, which is consistent with a renderer-independent cause.
live_prediction.requires: a live Google Docs qualification pass
